identity.name: Free City of Kraków
alt_names: Free, Independent and Strictly Neutral City of Cracow

land.text: 'created from the southwest part of the Duchy of Warsaw, on the left bank of the Vistula'

predecessors.note: Infobox 'Established: 3 May 1815'; the constitution was 'approved and guaranteed by Article VII of the treaty of 3 May 1815 between Austria, Prussia, and Russia'. duchy-of-warsaw records the loss in June 1815 (Final Act, 9 June).

land.text: 'Austria annexed the Free City on 16 November 1846 as the Grand Duchy of Kraków'

successors.note: The Grand Duchy of Kraków kept its own governorate commission but 'for administrative purposes' formed a single province with Galicia and Lodomeria (Grand Duchy of Kraków page).

keyframe_review.note: 1,645 km2 for 1815-1829 against the infobox 'Total area: 1,188.8 km2' (no year): ratio 1.38, within a factor of two; the Cliopatria polygon is the larger. The page describes 'Kraków and its environs, 224 villages, and three towns: Chrzanów, Trzebinia, and Nowa Góra', on the left bank of the Vistula, which matches the outline's size and position.

1,734 km2 for 1830-1833, 5 percent above the 1815 outline (23 vertices against 9). Unverified: page budget. None of the five pages opened gives a boundary change in 1830-33: the Free City page says only that Kraków served 'as a base for smuggling weapons' during the November Uprising and that in 1833 the three powers issued a more restrictive constitution; the November Uprising page does not mention Kraków. Probably a drafting difference in Cliopatria's polygon. Repair run: the Free City page re-read; it gives no boundary change for 1830-1833 (only the 1833 'new, much more restrictive constitution') and an area of 'between 1,164 and 1,234 km2 (sources vary)', so both outlines are 1.4 times the page's range; the 5 percent bump stays unexplained.

1,645 km2 for 1834-1841, the 1815 outline again. 'Cracow was occupied by the Austrian army from 1836 to 1841' and 'In 1836, the local police were disbanded and replaced by Austrian police' (Free City page): control tightened but the state's land is unchanged; the occupation is a ledger event here (occupation_start 1836, occupation_end 1841) and in austrian-empire.
1,645 km2 for 1842-1845, unchanged until the annexation of 16 November 1846.

correction.text: the 1842-1845 outline, for 1846 up to the annexation

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's row ends in 1845, but the Free City lasted until 'Austria annexed the Free City on 16 November 1846'. The shape is the 1842 outline, for the final year.

region.text: Kraków and its environs, 224 villages and three towns, from the southwest part of the Duchy of Warsaw

ledger.note: 3 May 1815: the Free City of Kraków is created from the Duchy of Warsaw. Infobox 'Established: 3 May 1815'; 'It comprised Kraków and its environs, 224 villages, and three towns: Chrzanów, Trzebinia, and Nowa Góra'; a 'nominally independent' city-state under Austria, Prussia and Russia. The Congress of Vienna page has Kraków become 'a free city as a shared protectorate of Austria, Prussia and Russia' without giving a date for it.

ledger.note: 1836: 'Cracow was subsequently occupied by the Austrian army from 1836 to 1841.' (Free City page; no month). The same page has the Free City's police disbanded and replaced by Austrian police in 1836. Mirrors austrian-empire/ledger/24.

region.text: the Free City of Kraków and its territory

ledger.note: 1841: end of the Austrian occupation ('from 1836 to 1841', Free City page; no month). Mirrors austrian-empire/ledger/25.
3 March 1846: 'Kraków was occupied first by Russians (on 3 March)'; the page adds that Davies writes the Russians joined the Austrians on 4 March.

March 1846: the Austrians arrived 'soon afterward (perhaps on the same day)' as the Russians (Kraków Uprising page); the day is the page's hedge, so confidence 2. The page does not say whether the occupiers stayed until the annexation.

16 November 1846: the protectorate ends when Austria annexes the Free City ('Austria annexed the Free City on 16 November 1846', Free City page); mirrors austrian-empire/ledger/26 (vassal_end 1846-11).

16 November 1846: the protectorate ends with the annexation. The Free City page: 'Austria unilaterally annexed the city-state'; the Kraków Uprising page has only Austria and Russia signing the 16 November treaty 'deciding to end the status of Kraków as the Free City', so Prussia's end rests on the end of the Free City itself (confidence 2).
16 November 1846: 'Austria and Russia signed a treaty on 16 November, deciding to end the status of Kraków as the Free City' (Kraków Uprising page); the protectorate ends with the annexation.
The Kraków Uprising page does not say when the Russian troops left. Recorded at the 16 November 1846 treaty, which ended the Free City, as a bridge over that silence.
16 November 1846: the occupation becomes annexation ('Austria annexed the Free City on 16 November 1846', Free City page; austrian-empire/ledger/27 records the gain).

16 November 1846: Austria annexes the Free City after the Kraków Uprising. 'After the 1846 Kraków Uprising, Austria annexed the Free City on 16 November 1846 as the Grand Duchy of Kraków.' The Kraków Uprising page says 'Austria and Russia signed a treaty on 16 November, deciding to end the status of Kraków as the Free City' and has the city annexed to the Kingdom of Galicia and Lodomeria.

16 November 1846: the Free City ends and becomes the Grand Duchy of Kraków. Grand Duchy page: 'created after the incorporation of the Free City of Cracow into Austria on 16 November 1846'; infobox 'Annexed: 16 November 1846'.

wars.name: November Uprising
wars.outcome: Organised resistance 'collapsed by October' 1831 (infobox 29 November 1830 - 21 October 1831); the Free City stayed outside the fighting.
wars.note: The November Uprising page never mentions the Free City. The Free City page says only that Kraków served 'as a base for smuggling weapons into the Russian-controlled Kingdom of Poland'. No occupation of Kraków in 1831 or 1833 is on any page opened.

wars.name: Kraków Uprising
belligerents: Polish insurgents (Provisional National Government of Kraków)
wars.outcome: 'The uprising lasted about nine days and ended with an Austrian victory'; Kraków was occupied first by Russians (3 March) and by Austrians 'perhaps on the same day'; Austria annexed the Free City on 16 November 1846.
wars.note: Infobox '21 February - 3 March 1846'; text 'began on the night of 20 February 1846'; provisional government formed 22 February. Davies gives 'Russians joined Austrians on 4 March'. The page names no Prussian occupation. Not turned into contest events: the insurgents held the city for days, not a front. The Russian and Austrian occupations of March to November 1846 are in the ledger.

certainty.note: A treaty-defined city-state with a described territory (the city, 224 villages, three towns); Cliopatria's polygon is coarse and about 38 percent larger than the infobox area.

notes: Written from five pages (budget up to 5). Cliopatria's four shapes differ only by a 5 percent bump in 1830-1833 that no page explains (kept ok, unverified: page budget). Area: Cliopatria 1,645 km2 against the infobox 1,188.8 km2 (no year), ratio 1.38. Dates: the Free City page and the Grand Duchy page give establishment 3 May 1815 (treaty of Austria, Prussia and Russia); austrian-empire and duchy-of-warsaw date it 9 June 1815 (Final Act); the Congress of Vienna page opened here gives no Kraków date. This dossier uses 3 May 1815 as the page infobox does. The Kraków Uprising page says Austria and Russia signed the 16 November treaty, not three powers; the Free City page says Austria annexed alone. Not on the pages: Russian or Prussian occupation of Kraków in 1831 and 1833, the 1835 secret treaty's effect (the Free City page has it: Austria gained the right to occupy and annex), the 1818 constitution's changes of territory (none). No rulers list (the Senate's head Stanisław Wodzicki 1815-1831 is the only name given). Counterparts: poles (1830-33 neighbour in the seed) and the Russian partition are not tied to any event here. Repair run (2026-11-01, Free City page and Kraków Uprising page re-opened): added the protectorate (vassal_start 1815-5 and vassal_end 1846-11 for austrian-empire, kingdom-of-prussia and russian-empire, three pairs because the validator pairs by counterpart string); the Austrian occupation 1836-1841 (mirrors austrian-empire/ledger/24-25); the 1846 occupations: Russian from 3 March and Austrian from the same days, both ended at the 16 November 1846 annexation (the page gives no earlier withdrawal; the Russian end is confidence 1). The Free City page says Austria 'unilaterally annexed' the city, the Kraków Uprising page has Austria and Russia signing the treaty; Prussia is named in neither, so its vassal_end is confidence 2. kingdom-of-prussia and russian-empire carry no mirror of the protectorate (their dossiers belong to other batches).
